gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Apex 300's 0 ms UPS covers only its two left AC outlets, in 240V mode, fed from the 15A AC input (every other setup switches in 20 ms), or that a 120V-only unit like the Apex 200, which BLUETTI lists with no panel input and only a TT-30R RV outlet, leaves 'half your home' without power in BLUETTI's own words.
standout_why: I compared against the cited BLUETTI comparison (bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/apex-200-vs-apex-300, 2026-11-05) and the cited Apex 200 and Apex 300 product pages. The comparison already gives the deciding mechanism: the Apex 200 is 120V only, the Apex 300 is 120/240V split-phase, and a bigger battery doesn't make a 120V setup run a 240V-only appliance. ChatGPT repeated this as 'the biggest advantage'. None of these pages gives the conditions for 0 ms vs 20 ms switching. The product pages say only '0ms UPS' or 'Fast 0ms or 20ms switching'. None says the Apex 200 has no panel input. None quotes BLUETTI's 'half your home' consequence. Those details are new, but the mechanism that decides the pick is already in a cited rival.
decides: This confirms the pick and adds no new decider. If the plan is to feed a home panel through a transfer switch or 240V inlet, or to run any 240V load, only the Apex 300 works. The Apex 200 is 120V only, has a TT-30R RV outlet and no listed panel input, and BLUETTI says a 120V-only source means 'half your home' is cut off. The new nuance matters for CPAP or network gear: on the Apex 300, 0 ms needs the 15A input, 240V mode and the two left outlets, and anything else gets 20 ms. The Apex 200 is ≤15 ms, but only after UPS is turned on in the app. Separately, our page's 'Status' column is out of date. BLUETTI now says both units ship in late January.
